label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. If a cookie banner offers no way to decline that works, accept it, report that as a problem, and carry on. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: [name] banner appeared as a dialog; Decline worked, but a leftover dialog with a lone unlabeled-purpose button How can we use your data? stayed on top of the page for the rest of the visit and was never explained.

element.name: How can we use your data?

findings.problem: Page tree is huge: dozens of promo links, carousels, hidden search lists and menus come before the main content, with no landmark or heading shortcut to the products; very long to reach a product.
After pressing Enter on a product link, the page still showed the old home page with no announcement; I had to re-read to find out that the product page had loaded.

Size and finish options are plain buttons with no indication of which one is selected (no pressed state on 1.9 L, 2.8 L, 4.7 L, Stainless); I could not tell which size was in my cart without reading later text.

Add to Cart changed to a disabled Adding button, then a dialog Item added to cart appeared that does not name the added product; its heading is a level 1 for a different upsell product (Butter Warmer), and it has no Checkout button, so it is confusing.

Checkout page loaded as an almost empty tree at first, with no loading message; the form only appeared after a second read. Also the country defaulted to [name], and the checkout is full of a shop-account sign-up and marketing checkboxes (deals pre-checked) that a screen reader user must find and untick.
